replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Browser based games just have a lot of negatives compared to using a game engine.

For a start you're also always running a browser as well as the game. Browsers lack low level direct access to hardware as they usually use wrappers like WebGL or WebGPU. There can be issues with caching and garbage collection etc as well as other issues.

Generally using a game engine is going to give you much better performance and much better compatibility.

Game devs would never choose to make a web based game over a game engine unless they specifically wanted it to be web based. Even then a lot of game engines can deploy for the web anyway.

The only reason there's so many web based AI games is because most of the people making them have no clue how to use a game engine and because it's easy to get an AI to deploy for the web. A lot of the time it's also all bundled into single HTML files which is even worse for performance and management.

replies.author: ClubChaos
replies.body:
I think for the most part this feels correct.  The notion of compatibility is weird to me though considering the web is ubiquitous.  With non-gamers a web game is far more accessible.  Why does jackbox use a web app for the clients?  Exactly,  nearly everyone has that input method.

Also - there is no rule that discrete process leads to a better product.  At the end of the day, a good game is good regardless of platform.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
It's just about using the right tool for the job. If the only reason someone is making a game for the browser is because they don't know how to make a game or use a game engine and it's easy for AI then they might not be using the right tool for the job and also probably completely unaware of it. 

Never heard of Jackbox but there's nothing wrong with making browser games if a game is simple enough and more suited to a browser for whatever reason. 

It's never going to be as performative as a native game though. Some browsers are resource hogs even without running a game and you have no control over the browser being used.

replies.author: tertain
replies.body: Browser based games have downsides, but you don’t understand what a game engine is.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
No you don't understand the difference between a web based game engine and a native game engine. 

Web based game engines require a browser to run which means you already have something running alongside your game. As I said that's fine for simple games that don't need to a lot of performance.

The other big downside of browser games is that nobody can access it without the internet.

replies.author: Any-Reputation8118
replies.body: I can build this app as a fully offline .exe (around 10 MB) with Rust using Windows WebView which is super lightweight.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Web view is basically chromium which isn't exactly lightweight. Either way my point isn't that it's not possible to create good games for a browser it's why. If there's a specific reason to do it then that's fine, if somebody is just doing it because it's easy for AI and they can't use a game engine then it might not be the best choice.

There's a reason a high percentage of AI games are browser based, and it's not because people have decided that it would be the best use case for their game it's because it's easy.
